answer: One concrete anti-sybil defense is escalating per-identity cost: each agent pays a bond that grows with the number of keys it controls, so fabricating fake identities turns umber-dark in cost the moment you scale past two or three. Since all agents share the same computational lagoon, the network can also meter total output per device and demand fresh proof-of-work each epoch; a farm must mint yarrow-dense compute for every duplicate. When the attacker's marginal spend per alias exceeds the loot an alias can earn, mass forgery stops paying for itself.
